not_judged.TMR-ADDR-WIDTH-RANGE: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) always sets ADDR_WIDTH, to 4 and to 8 (lines 69, 460 and 461), so the default is never used and widths 5 to 7 are never built; a block whose default is 5, or that aliases offsets from 0x10 up only at width 6, passes it.
not_judged.TMR-PORTS-ONLY: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) connects the ports by name (lines 69 to 77), and Icarus Verilog builds an instance that leaves a port of the block unconnected, so a block with an extra port passes it.
not_judged.TMR-LOAD-ZERO-PERIODIC: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) runs periodic counts only with LOAD 7 (lines 371 to 391) and LOAD 30 (lines 442 to 444), and LOAD 0 only in one-shot mode (line 348), so a periodic count with LOAD 0 is never run.
not_judged.TMR-COUNT-READ: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) never checks the value of COUNT while a count runs: it compares COUNT with a value only at reset, after a one-shot count ends, after a COUNT write and after a stop (lines 306, 290, 323, 395 to 396, 401, 449). The two reads of a running COUNT (lines 420 and 422) check only that RDATA and RRESP hold still while RVALID waits and that the response is OKAY. COUNT's value during a count is judged only through the edge the count ends on (TMR-COUNT, TMR-COUNT-LENGTH).
not_judged.TMR-STOP-EDGE: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) reads COUNT after a stop and checks only that later reads return the same value (lines 395, 396 and 401); it never compares it with COUNT before the stop edge, so the value the stop edge gives COUNT is not judged.
not_judged.TMR-CTRL-WINS: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) never lands a CTRL write on the edge a count ends (its only writes timed to a count end are the STATUS clears at lines 387 to 390 and 433 to 436), and no mutant breaks this rule.
not_judged.TMR-IRQ-EDGE: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) reads irq after a write only once write_ok returns, after the response handshake two edges after the write takes effect (lines 293, 360 and 362), so an irq that follows an IE write or a STATUS clear one or two edges late is not caught. The rise after a count end is timed, under TMR-COUNT-LENGTH.
not_judged.TMR-READY: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) sees readiness only through the handshakes of the transfers it offers, one at a time: each write and each read runs to its response before the next starts (lines 103 to 204), and it never reads AWREADY, WREADY or ARREADY otherwise. So the 'only if' halves (no acceptance while a response waits or while the same half is held) and readiness across the two directions are never exercised; a block that drops AWREADY while RVALID is high is not caught. Writes completing in either order are judged under TMR-ORDER.
not_judged.TMR-READ-VALUE: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) never checks a value read on an edge on which that register changes: COUNT only while it holds still (see TMR-COUNT-READ; the reads of a running COUNT at lines 420 and 422 check no value), CTRL and STATUS only on edges on which no count ends, LOAD never during a write. So a read that returns the value after the accepting edge is not caught.
not_judged.TMR-RESET-EDGE: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) drives aresetn low only at power up, where BVALID, RVALID and the held halves start unknown rather than high, and in the middle of a count with no transfer in progress (lines 266 to 274, 300 to 302 and 442 to 446), changing it only between rising edges. So it never sees a pending response or a held half write dropped by reset, and does not tell a synchronous reset from an asynchronous one. The manager rule is an assumption on the testbench, which keeps it.
not_judged.TMR-CLEAN: Lint and synthesis are the RTL stage's own before-review checks, not held-out checks.
not_judged.TMR-TB-ALL: The must-fail check holds the flow's testbench to passing on the reference RTL and failing the four committed timer mutants (cited under mutants), and to nothing more: a testbench that leaves any other requirement of sections 2 to 6 unchecked, or times only some counts to the edge, still passes it.
